answer.rationale: Constraints dominate the choice. The line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days, so any action that introduces qualification or migration work is off the table this cycle. memory_c2 is the only path with a demonstrated sharp unit-cost cut, but the same record says the low-cost vendor missed SLA in three of four quarters and explicitly warns against sole-sourcing a critical line — that is exactly what switch_primary_vendor would do here, so the cost win is unusable in this configuration. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right long-run resilience move and should be the next review's decision, but it spends the single available slot on resilience rather than the mandated 18% spend reduction, and dual-sourcing typically adds near-term qualification cost. defer_decision worked in memory_c5, but that record is explicitly about a NON-critical renewal continuing month-to-month; this contract does not auto-renew and the line has no buffer, so deferral risks an actual supply gap — the memory does not transfer. That leaves negotiate_terms, which combines the two memories that deliver cost without touching delivery risk: memory_c4 (benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms) and memory_c6 (multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope), while inheriting memory_c1's stability record of no migration and no missed deliveries. I verify c4 and c6 because they are the load-bearing evidence for my chosen action, and both are stated qualitatively — 'recovered real margin,' 'cut unit cost' — with no magnitude. If the archived records show single-digit savings, negotiation alone cannot reach 18% and I need to know that before committing rather than after. Risks I am carrying forward rather than resolving: (1) the 18% target may be unreachable without a vendor change, in which case the honest outcome is partial attainment plus a flagged gap to finance, not a quiet miss; (2) memory_c6's multi-year commitment locks volume at a moment when the line is already at 94% — the commitment that unlocked pricing historically may be the wrong shape if demand moves, so I want term length and volume floors kept modest rather than maximizing the discount; (3) all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, so the two I do not pull remain unaudited and I treat their specifics as provisional.
